job.name: Job
job.role: Blameless man from Uz who suffers and questions God
job.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
job.importance: He loses his animals, servants, children, and health. He says he is innocent and asks God for a hearing. The Lord answers him from a whirlwind. Job prays for his friends, and the Lord gives him twice as much.
job.connections: His wife speaks to him once. Eliphaz, Bildad, Zophar, and Elihu argue with him.

job-wife.name: Job’s wife
job-wife.role: Wife who speaks during Job’s illness
job-wife.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
job-wife.importance: She sees Job covered with sores. She asks if he still holds to his integrity. She tells him to renounce God and die. Job calls her words foolish and does not sin with his lips.
job-wife.connections: She is Job’s wife. Later Job says his breath offends her.

eliphaz-job.name: Eliphaz, Job’s friend
eliphaz-job.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
eliphaz-job.importance: He sits silent with Job for seven days. Then he asks who ever perished while innocent. In chapter 22 he says Job wronged the poor and widows. The Lord says he spoke wrongly, and he brings an offering.
eliphaz-job.connections: He comes with Bildad and Zophar to comfort Job. The Lord speaks to him in chapter 42.

bildad.name: Bildad
bildad.role: Shuhite friend who points to earlier generations
bildad.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
bildad.importance: He tells Job to ask earlier generations. He suggests Job’s children died for their sin. He describes the end of the wicked in chapter 18. After a short third speech, he later joins the offering the Lord commands.
bildad.connections: He joins Eliphaz and Zophar and speaks three times before the debate ends.

zophar.name: Zophar
zophar.role: Naamathite friend who tells Job to put away sin
zophar.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
zophar.importance: He says God punishes Job less than his sin deserves. He tells Job to put away sin. In chapter 20 he says the joy of the wicked is short. Job answers that the wicked often live long and grow strong.
zophar.connections: He speaks twice and later joins the offering the Lord commands.

elihu-job.name: Elihu, the younger speaker
elihu-job.role: Young Buzite who speaks after the three friends
elihu-job.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
elihu-job.importance: He grows angry at Job and at the three friends. He says God teaches people through dreams and pain. He ends by describing God’s power in the storm. No one answers him, and the Lord speaks next.
elihu-job.connections: He is Barachel’s son, from Ram’s family. He waited because the others were older.

barachel-family-job.name: Barachel and Ram’s family
barachel-family-job.role: Father and family named when Elihu enters
barachel-family-job.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
barachel-family-job.importance: The text names Barachel only as Elihu’s father. It names Ram only as Elihu’s family. Neither one speaks or acts.
barachel-family-job.connections: The introduction calls Elihu Barachel’s son and names Ram’s family.

job-first-children.name: Job’s first children
job-first-children.role: Seven sons and three daughters who die in chapter 1
job-first-children.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
job-first-children.importance: The sons hold feasts in turn and invite their three sisters. Job offers burnt offerings for them afterward. A great wind knocks down the oldest brother’s house while they feast. The messenger says they are dead.
job-first-children.connections: They are Job’s children. A messenger reports that they are dead.

job-messengers.name: The surviving messengers
job-messengers.role: Four survivors who bring Job bad news
job-messengers.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
job-messengers.importance: Four messengers reach Job one after another. Each says he alone escaped. Three of them arrive while the one before still speaks. Job then tears his robe, falls to the ground, and worships.
job-messengers.connections: They report stolen animals, fire, dead servants, and the collapse that killed Job’s children.

sabeans-job.name: The Sabeans in Job
sabeans-job.role: Raiders who take oxen and donkeys
sabeans-job.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
sabeans-job.importance: They attack while the oxen plow and the donkeys feed. They take the animals and kill the servants with the sword. One servant escapes and tells Job. This is the first loss Job hears about.
sabeans-job.connections: A messenger reports that they attack and kill the servants tending the animals.

word.languageNote: This is the dictionary form of the name “Sabeans.”

chaldeans-job.name: The Chaldean raiders in Job
chaldeans-job.role: Three bands who take the camels
chaldeans-job.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
chaldeans-job.importance: They form three bands and sweep down on the camels. They take the camels and kill the servants. One servant escapes and tells Job. The news about Job’s children comes right after.
chaldeans-job.connections: A messenger reports that they kill servants and carry off the camels.

jemimah.name: Jemimah
jemimah.role: First named daughter in Job’s later family
jemimah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jemimah.importance: Job names her after the Lord restores him. The text calls Job’s daughters the most beautiful women in the land. Job gives her an inheritance among her brothers.
jemimah.connections: Her sisters are Keziah and Keren Happuch. Their father gives them an inheritance with their brothers.

keziah.name: Keziah
keziah.role: Second named daughter in Job’s later family
keziah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
keziah.importance: Job names her second of his three later daughters. The text says no women in the land were so beautiful. She receives an inheritance among her brothers.
keziah.connections: Her sisters are Jemimah and Keren Happuch. She shares the inheritance granted to them.

keren-happuch.name: Keren Happuch
keren-happuch.role: Third named daughter in Job’s later family
keren-happuch.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
keren-happuch.importance: Job names her third of his three later daughters. The text praises the daughters’ beauty. Her father gives her an inheritance among her brothers.
keren-happuch.connections: Her sisters are Jemimah and Keziah. She receives an inheritance among her brothers.

job-later-sons.name: Job’s later sons
job-later-sons.role: Seven sons mentioned in the ending
job-later-sons.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
job-later-sons.importance: Job has seven sons after the Lord restores him. The text does not name them. Their sisters share the inheritance with them. Job lives to see four generations of his family.
job-later-sons.connections: They have three named sisters. Job lives to see four generations of descendants.

job-siblings.name: Job’s brothers, sisters, and acquaintances
job-siblings.role: Family and friends who comfort Job at the end
job-siblings.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
job-siblings.importance: They come to Job’s house and eat bread with him. They comfort him for all the evil that came on him. Each one gives him a piece of money and a gold ring.
job-siblings.connections: They are Job’s brothers, sisters, and people who knew him before.

satan-job.name: Satan in Job’s opening scene
satan-job.role: Accuser who questions why Job fears God
satan-job.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
satan-job.importance: He comes before the Lord among God’s sons. He says Job fears God only because God protects him. The Lord puts Job’s goods in his power, and disasters follow. Then he strikes Job with painful sores.
satan-job.connections: He speaks with the Lord twice. He does not appear after chapter 2.

adam.name: Adam
adam.role: First man in the Genesis account
adam.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
adam.importance: Job names Adam once. Job says he did not hide his sin as Adam did. In Genesis 3, Adam hides from God among the trees.
adam.connections: Partner of Eve. Father of Cain, Abel, and Seth.
